review_notes:
I read all of TranslationC1.lean (lines 1–110), plus the files it depends on: Definitions.lean (`CounterexampleManifold`, `CounterexampleAmbient`, `standardEmbedding`, `IsC1SelfMap`), Embedding.lean (`continuous_of_local_contDiff_extension`, `isC1SelfMap_of_contDiff`) and SphereTranslation.lean (`denom`, `ambient`, `domain`, `contDiffOn_ambient`, `denom_pos`). A grep shows that `HasLocalExtension`, `translateCoordinate` and the three theorems are not used anywhere else in the repository. SphereGeometry.lean imports the file but does not reference these names.

The main theorem `isC1SelfMap_translateCoordinate` is already stated at the right level of generality: it asks only for a local C¹ extension of the coefficient and a C¹ self-map `f`. The ℝ/ℂ scalars come from the concrete counterexample manifold. Abstracting them would hide the result and is not needed.

The one finding concerns the two convenience wrappers. They require the coefficient `D` to be C¹ on the whole ambient space, but the proof only uses C¹ regularity on an open set containing the embedded manifold. I have not compiled the proposed replacement. The proof sketch uses only the definitions shown here and the existing `isC1SelfMap_translateCoordinate`.

findings.excerpt:
(D : CounterexampleAmbient q → ℂ) (hD : ContDiff ℝ 1 D) :
    HasLocalExtension q (fun y => D (standardEmbedding q y)) := by
findings.problem: Both wrappers require `D` to be C¹ on all of `CounterexampleAmbient q`. The proof uses `Set.univ` as the open set, but `HasLocalExtension` only asks, for each point of the manifold, for an open set containing that point's embedding on which `D` is C¹. The manifold is `StandardClock × (Fin (q+1) → StandardSphere2)`. Its embedding lies in a set that stays away from the origin in every factor. Natural coefficient functions on the ambient space, such as ones built from `1/‖x‖`, a normalisation, or a quotient like `SphereTranslation.denom`/`chart` with a nonvanishing denominator, are C¹ only on an open neighbourhood of the manifold, not on all of the ambient space. To use these wrappers with such a `D`, a user would first have to extend it globally (for example with bump functions) or fall back to unfolding `HasLocalExtension` by hand.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the global hypothesis with C¹ regularity on an open set that contains the embedded manifold:

theorem hasLocalExtension_of_contDiffOn {q : ℕ}
    (D : CounterexampleAmbient q → ℂ) {U : Set (CounterexampleAmbient q)}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hrange : ∀ y, standardEmbedding q y ∈ U)
    (hD : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 D U) :
    HasLocalExtension q (fun y => D (standardEmbedding q y)) :=
  fun x => ⟨U, hU, hrange x, D, hD, fun _ _ => rfl⟩

Give `isC1SelfMap_translateCoordinate_of_contDiffOn` the same hypotheses `(hU) (hrange) (hD)` and prove it with `isC1SelfMap_translateCoordinate i (hasLocalExtension_of_contDiffOn D hU hrange hD) hf`. The current global statements become the special case `U = Set.univ`, via `isOpen_univ`, `fun _ => Set.mem_univ _` and `hD.contDiffOn`. They can be kept as one-line corollaries if desired. The proof needs nothing new: it is the existing anonymous constructor with `Set.univ` replaced by `U`. Degenerate cases are unchanged. `q` is any natural number, the manifold is nonempty, and the condition on `U` is just `Set.range (standardEmbedding q) ⊆ U`.
findings.benefit: With this change the convenience wrapper covers the coefficient functions most likely to occur in this construction, which are typically smooth only near the sphere or circle factors. Users no longer need a global smooth extension or to unfold `HasLocalExtension` by hand. The statement is no harder to read, and the proof stays a one-liner.
